newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shangri-La confident on 1997 prospects.
newsitem.headline: Shangri-La confident on 1997 prospects.

text.p: Shangri-La Asia Ltd managing director Paul Bush said the hotel group is confident about its Hong Kong and China prospects for 1997.
"We are still optimistic that 1997 will be a satisfactory year in China," Shangri-La managing director Paul Bush told reporters after the company's annual meeting on Friday.
He said the group's Hong Kong hotels were booked out for the the territory's handover period. Hong Kong reverts to China at midnight of June 30, after more than 150 years of British rule.
While there was a fall in bookings immediately after the handover, particularly July and August, he expected a pick-up later in 1997, helped by international events in the territory.
"We still look to the complete 1997 year in Hong Kong with confidence," Bush said.
Hong Kong is hosting a World Bank/International Monetary Fund meeting in September which is expected to attract at least 10,000 visitors to the territory.
Earlier, Shangri-La chairman Liu Tai-fung said 1996 had seen a fall in business arrivals in China, particularly in Beijing and Shanghai, and shorter lengths of stay.
Liu predicted strong revenue growth fuelled by the region's expanding economies, despite some start-up losses at new hotels.
